# Requirements

Build HyperMind: a Rust memory kernel that fuses the neocortex ledger discipline (encrypted, tamper-evident, deterministic, bitemporal) with the cortex-engine cognitive loop (ingest, consolidate, forget, believe, adjudicate) and the harness lessons (evidence authority, required bindings, attention-gated anticipation, generations, byte-range citations, protected self). The system is a stack of eight layers and is built as eight vertical slices, each adding to every layer and ending in a runnable end-to-end journey. No wave builds one layer alone. Every wave ships an eval gate. The agent that uses HyperMind resumes where it left off, knows when things were true, notices when it is wrong, anticipates without interrupting, learns procedures from independent episodes, and proves where every recalled fact came from, on every turn, in under 10 ms, with no LLM on the hot path.

## Requirement 1: Vertical build discipline

**User Story:** As the owner, I need the engine built as slices through every layer so that each wave is a working system, never an unproven layer waiting for its consumer.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every wave adds to every layer it touches and ends with an integration task whose journey test crosses schema, ledger, projections, indexes, cognition where present, compose, MCP or SDK, restart and recall. Lane tasks in wave N+1 require the integration task of wave N.
2. No task delivers behaviour in a crate that no task in the same wave consumes. Empty scaffolding crates from task 1.1 are the only exception. cg spec render and the wave graph reflect this dependency shape.
3. Each wave's eval gate is added in that wave and runs in CI before the wave closes.

## Requirement 2: Ledger durability and idempotency

**User Story:** As an agent runtime, I need every accepted write to survive any crash and never apply twice.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Frames carry a 43-byte header and CRC32C; segments use group commit with fdatasync and a manifest; open repairs a torn tail and refuses interior corruption with kInteriorCorruption. The neocortex frame and segment test vectors pass unchanged.
2. Append is idempotent by connection id and client sequence with strictly sequential admission; an exact replay returns duplicate; a same-sequence different-digest replay is kIdempotencyConflict; the dedup map rebuilds from envelope metadata at boot; a torn multi-event batch is rolled back at open.
3. The fault simulator converges to identical CanonicalBytes over 2,048 schedules including torn writes, reordered completions, lying fsync and kill after every durable LSN; a real fork and SIGKILL test after commit passes.

## Requirement 3: Sealing, integrity and verification

**User Story:** As an operator, I need memory encrypted at rest, tamper-evident without keys, and erasable with a receipt.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every payload is sealed with XChaCha20-Poly1305 and AAD bound to actor, lsn, kind and user; plaintext on disk is refused; keys are zeroised on close; rotation re-wraps the data key without rewriting the log.
2. The MMR leaf commits to the sealed bytes; checkpoints are Ed25519-signed; hm verify audits an actor directory offline with no key and prints the root and LSN; VerifyStatus reports the same online; every append ack returns leaf count, leaf hash and root.
3. CryptoDelete writes a signed deletion receipt containing the key fingerprint and root, unlinks the keyring, and a reopen reports kKeyDestroyed. Tripwire LSNs held by the kernel raise a security event on any activation, retract or forget.

## Requirement 4: Evidence authority and anti-laundering

**User Story:** As a user, I need the agent to know what was observed, what was asserted and what was inferred, and to be unable to promote one into another.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every event and every surfaced item carries one of six authority classes set at ingest from source kind. A derived record is derived_inference unless its text is a verbatim quote of a cited byte range. A model-authored string cannot gain tool_observed by passing through a tool.
2. Outcome and LoopClosed done events must cite tool_observed, external_observed or runtime_fact LSNs; citing a memory, summary or reconstruction is rejected at admission. memory.* events are never re-ingested.
3. Renderers never place memory content in the system or developer role, drop items without full provenance, exclude same-turn content and raw bytes, and label authority on every item. The laundering suite reports zero violations.

## Requirement 5: Projections and generations

**User Story:** As the kernel, I need every read model rebuildable from the log and every consolidation publishable and retractable atomically.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Each projection applies in one LMDB write transaction that commits mutations and its checkpoint together and requires applied_lsn equals checkpoint plus one; rebuild from any prefix yields byte-identical CanonicalDump; a SIGKILL mid-rebuild resumes from the minimum checkpoint.
2. A consolidation run stages derived events under run_id into a generation; publish is a compare-and-swap on active_generation that refuses if any staged record lacks a projection; readers lease a generation for a bounded time; retractions apply to every generation including leased ones; retract switches the pointer back without waiting for cleanup.
3. Projections present at v1.0: timeline, lexical, entities, vectors, beliefs, graph, memories, fsrs, intent frame, bindings, work ledger, intentions, attention history, predictions, procedures, attestations, temporal ladder, runs.

## Requirement 6: Retrieval lanes and planner

**User Story:** As an agent, I need recall that finds paraphrases, exact identifiers, time windows and connected ideas, and explains why.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Lexical uses fixed-point BM25 over tantivy postings; vector uses a binary prefilter then int8 dot products with SIMD equal to scalar, flat below 50k and HNSW above with measured recall parity; entity uses exact postings for ids, paths, urls and proper nouns; temporal descends the ladder; graph walks validated edges with validity intervals; belief reads as-of heads.
2. The planner classifies query shape deterministically and selects lanes and weights; fusion is reciprocal rank over canonical ids; the composite multiplies fsrs retrievability, salience factor and recency prior; every hit carries a provenance URI with lane ranks and a why code.
3. recall@10 is at least 0.95 on the 10k seeded store; recall supports modes semantic, lexical, entity, temporal, graph, asof, timeline and reconstruct, and near for anchored retrieval.

## Requirement 7: Activation bundle and deadline

**User Story:** As an agent runtime, I need a budgeted, ordered, explainable context on every turn that never blocks the turn.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Ten tiers in shed order with resident, intent, bindings and work_ledger required and never shed; exact token counts per target model; trim sheds from the tail and coarsens conversation items before required tiers; if required tiers exceed budget the bundle narrows the subtask and reports a gap.
2. The bundle is canonically serialised as HMA1, hashed, pinned to a snapshot epoch, carries a RetrievalManifest with candidates, selected, included and used, plus gaps and health; every provenance LSN yields an Attestation frame.
3. activate p99 is under 10 ms at 100k events warm; on a deadline miss it returns the last bundle marked degraded with stale_by_lsn and pushes the fresh bundle over Subscribe; the silent-degradation suite shows every forced miss in gaps or health.

## Requirement 8: Beliefs and time

**User Story:** As a user, I need the agent to know what was true when, what it knew when, and to surface contradictions unprompted.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Beliefs are versioned with supersedes chains, conflict edges with obligated surfacing, and as-of queries by valid_at or known_at that can return different answers; records are tri-temporal with event_time_ns, observation LSN and validity.
2. The admission gate rejects negative_existence without a corroborating tool_observed LSN and lists same-domain conflicts before commit; identity, constraint and preference accept Assertion and Retract only from user or admin authority; runs emit ProposedAssertion surfaced in the conflicts tier.
3. dispute runs in-process NLI both directions, escalates genuine to one tier-capped LLM supersession check, and yields Retract plus Assertion or a conflict edge; the temporal suite reports zero stale facts stated as current.

## Requirement 9: Consolidation as retractable generations

**User Story:** As a user, I need the agent to consolidate what it learns without ever corrupting what it knew, and to undo any consolidation.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. NREM clusters without an LLM and makes one structured-output call per cluster; REM connects from adjacency with one long-context pass, abstracts with novelty and grounding gates, and audits with hindsight defaulting to no change; every derived record carries run_id, model_provenance and citations.
2. Every quoted span in a derived record lies inside a cited byte range in the run's frozen candidate set or the candidate is dropped and counted; mint requires at least three independent source roots from at least two conversations; derived authority is derived_inference.
3. Runs declare max_llm_calls, max_tokens, max_usd and max_wall_ms and abort cleanly on any; phases persist with a per-attempt idempotency prefix and resume after a crash; consolidate retract switches activation back immediately; the dream regression fixture shows zero lossy rewrites.

## Requirement 10: Retention and forgetting

**User Story:** As a user, I need the agent to forget noise and never forget what it is standing on.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. FSRS-6 orders review from attestations, retrieval rank and contradiction involvement; dreams do not count as access.
2. Retention class in current_state, daily, durable, do_not_store decides eligibility; do_not_store writes nothing; the protection set excludes provenance of open loops, active bindings, unfulfilled intentions, resident beliefs and the last N bundles; the last K contradicted outcomes per domain are kept as counterexamples.
3. Fading is an event; faded memories are excluded from refine, connect, abstract and sampling; nothing is deleted except by crypto-shred or an explicit retract.

## Requirement 11: Prospective memory and attention

**User Story:** As a user, I want the agent to follow up on its own, and to know when not to interrupt me.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. IntentionSet accepts the wake-trigger vocabulary; triggers are persisted before the action waits; IntentionFired carries a stable wake id so duplicate external events resume once.
2. Every fired intention is scored by the attention function with quiet hours, notification budget and workload applied and recorded as AttentionDecided with a readable reason; only notify, ask_user and start_work reach the prospective tier; batch produces a digest item; schedule re-arms.
3. The attention history is a bounded projection the user can inspect; attention suppression precision on the labelled set is at least 0.9.

## Requirement 12: Predictions and procedures

**User Story:** As a user, I want the agent to say what it expects, notice when it was wrong, and get better at things it has done before.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Predicted carries bounded predicates from the fixed vocabulary and a deadline; OutcomeObserved assesses supported, contradicted, pending, unresolvable or not_executed with observation LSNs; calibration is reported per predicate kind; a revision_required gap follows three same-mechanism failures.
2. Procedures are mined from ToolCall to ToolResult to Effect to Outcome chains per closed loop; supported requires three independent source roots from two conversations; adopted requires a user-authority event; only adopted procedures render as instructions, tentative ones render as observations.
3. Model narrative cannot redefine success after results; assessments cite observation LSNs only.

## Requirement 13: Surfaces

**User Story:** As an integrator, I need one protocol locally and remotely, thirteen composable tools, a REST mirror and a CLI.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The Unix socket speaks NCPR framing byte-compatible with neocortex proto_version 2 and adds v3 requests; gRPC over mTLS carries the same envelope bytes with streaming Subscribe; admin and actor tokens are disjoint and never mix on a connection.
2. MCP exposes exactly the thirteen verbs with the one envelope; every mutation error carries effect_state; resources resolve hm:// URIs; a prompt exposes the activate-backed system block; REST mirrors the verbs with OpenAPI and gates destructive verbs on the admin token.
3. hm covers init, serve, doctor, actor management, remember, recall, activate, consolidate, verify, bench, export, import and tui; every command takes --json.

## Requirement 14: SDKs and migration

**User Story:** As a developer, I need HyperMind from Rust, TypeScript, Python and Go with one contract, and a path off cortex-engine.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The Rust crate is the kernel with an embedded API; TypeScript ships engine via napi prebuilds, client over gRPC and mcp; Python ships hypermind via maturin wheels and a gRPC client; the Go client keeps its sequence-recovery state machine and gains Recall, AsOf, Subscribe and CryptoDelete builders; all pass their suites against the real daemon.
2. Every SDK exposes Session, remember, recall, activate to Bundle, render, attest, believe, intend, bind, predict, outcome and consolidate with the same envelope and error codes; every mutation error carries effect_state; renderers enforce activation safety.
3. migrate-from-cortex imports a cortex-engine SQLite or JSON store into events with authority user_asserted for observations and derived_inference for dream-minted memories, preserves ids and edges, and verifies counts and a sample of embeddings.

## Requirement 15: Evaluation gate and targets

**User Story:** As the owner, I need every quality claim to be a number produced in CI.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. hm-eval runs the internal suites and the public benchmarks, writes JSON to eval/results, compares against main with per-metric tolerance, and fails CI on regression; judge models are pinned and responses cached by content hash; judge-free and judged metrics are reported separately.
2. Wave 8 publishes LongMemEval at least 90 percent, LoCoMo at least 75 percent F1, recall@10 at least 0.95 at 10k, activate p99 under 10 ms at 100k warm, zero lossy rewrites, zero stale facts, zero laundering violations, continuity 100 percent, determinism 100 percent across x86-64 and aarch64, attention precision at least 0.9, and cost per 1k turns.
3. A hash-feature embedder is labelled lexical_only in every report; no metric is blended across encoders or judges.

## Requirement 16: Documentation and packaging

**User Story:** As an adopter, I need to add memory to any MCP client in two commands and understand what it does.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. docs contain start-here, concepts, guides, reference (schematics rewritten from the schema, protocol, MCP, CLI, config, prompts, SDKs), internals, evaluation, security and ADRs; every public type and tool carries when-to-use and do-not-use; the docs gate passes.
2. Packaging ships a distroless static image, compose, systemd unit and Helm chart; models download on first run with pinned digests; hm doctor reports what is present; release builds are reproducible.

## Requirement 17: Multi-actor isolation and budgets

**User Story:** As an operator, I need many agents in one daemon without leakage and with bounded cost.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Actors have separate keys, logs, LMDB environments and vector lanes; one writer task per actor; cross-actor reads happen only through bridges that append origin_actor events or a read-only commons actor.
2. Per-connection output queues are bounded and a saturated subscriber is disconnected; consolidation runs per actor under declared budgets; cost is accounted per operation and reported.
